questions.stem: A structured data extraction system achieves 97% overall accuracy across all document types. The team proposes automating all extractions where model confidence exceeds 95% to reduce human review costs. What is the critical risk in this approach?

options.text: The 95% confidence threshold is too low and should be raised to 99% for automation
options.explanation: The threshold value is not the core issue — the problem is that aggregate metrics hide per-type performance disparities.

options.text: Aggregate accuracy can mask poor per-type performance, and confidence scores need calibration before use.
options.explanation: 97% overall can hide 40% error rates on specific document types. Without stratified validation and confidence calibration, automation will silently fail on certain inputs.

options.text: The model will become overconfident over time as it processes more documents, requiring regular retraining
options.explanation: LLMs do not train during inference. The issue is existing calibration gaps, not drift.

options.text: Automated extractions should always have human review regardless of confidence, making the proposal fundamentally flawed
options.explanation: Automation is valid when properly validated — the issue is doing it based on uncalibrated aggregate metrics, not the concept of automation itself.

questions.rationale: 97% overall can hide 40% error rates on specific document types. Without stratified validation and confidence calibration, automation will silently fail on certain inputs.

sources.label: Lesson 5.5: Human Review and Confidence Calibration (Aggregate metrics trap)

questions.stem: A documentation team working across a 500,000-line codebase notices that Claude Code's responses become less specific after extensive file exploration. What is the term for this degradation and what is the primary mitigation in Claude Code?

options.text: Token exhaustion, mitigated by raising max_tokens so the model has room to keep referencing every file it has read.
options.explanation: max_tokens controls response length, not the model's ability to retain and reference earlier context. The degradation occurs because verbose exploration output fills the context window, not because responses are truncated.

options.text: Context degradation, mitigated by scratchpad files and by delegating verbose exploration to subagents.
options.explanation: Context degradation occurs when the model loses grip on specific details as verbose tool output accumulates in the conversation. Scratchpad files persist findings on disk where they can be re-read as needed. Subagent delegation isolates verbose exploration output from the main agent's context budget.

options.text: Hallucination drift — mitigated by lowering the temperature to zero for deterministic output
options.explanation: The issue is not hallucination from randomness but loss of specificity from context overload. Temperature zero produces deterministic output but does not help the model retain specific findings from earlier in a long context.

options.text: Prompt injection — mitigated by sanitising file contents before they enter the context window
options.explanation: Prompt injection is a security concern involving malicious content in inputs. The described problem — responses becoming vague after extensive exploration — is context degradation from accumulated verbose output, not a security issue.

questions.rationale: Context degradation occurs when the model loses grip on specific details as verbose tool output accumulates in the conversation. Scratchpad files persist findings on disk where they can be re-read as needed. Subagent delegation isolates verbose exploration output from the main agent's context budget.

sources.label: Lesson 5.4: Codebase Exploration and Context Degradation

questions.stem: Your extraction pipeline uses tool_use with a JSON schema, so outputs always parse. Finance still reports invoices where line items do not sum to the stated total, and where the due date precedes the invoice date. The team wants retries to receive precise, per-field error messages. What should you add?

options.text: Tighter JSON schema constraints: numeric minimum and maximum bounds on every amount field and format checks on every date field
options.explanation: Range and format constraints check fields in isolation; both reported failures are relationships between fields, which a JSON schema cannot express.

options.text: An instruction telling the model to double-check its own extraction in the same request before responding
options.explanation: Same-session self-review retains the generation context and its bias, and produces no machine-readable error for the retry loop to feed back.

options.text: A Pydantic model whose validators encode the sum and date-order rules, feeding its validation errors into retries
options.explanation: Cross-field semantic rules live in validation code; Pydantic validators express them and raise per-field errors the retry request can quote verbatim.

options.text: A more capable model, since semantic errors indicate the current one is under-powered
options.explanation: No model tier guarantees semantic correctness; the fix is validation logic around the model, and an upgrade is the maximum-cost non-answer.

questions.rationale: The schema already eliminated syntax errors; what remains is semantic validation. Cross-field rules cannot be expressed in a JSON schema, so they live in validation code. A Pydantic model with custom validators encodes them and raises specific, per-field error messages that feed the retry-with-error-feedback loop.
questions.conflictNote: La guía resuelve el mismo síntoma (ítems que no suman al total) con stated_total vs calculated_total y revisión humana, no con un validador que alimenta reintentos.

sources.label: Lesson 4.4: Validation, Retry, and Feedback Loops (Pydantic as the validation layer)

questions.stem: Your Claude Code setup reviews generated code by asking the same model instance to critique its own output immediately after generation, within the same conversation. The team notices the reviews are overly favourable and miss bugs that an external reviewer would catch. What is the root cause and correct fix?

options.text: The model needs more detailed review instructions; add a comprehensive checklist of what to look for during self-review
options.explanation: More detailed instructions do not overcome the fundamental limitation. The model retains its reasoning context from generation and is less likely to question its own decisions regardless of how detailed the checklist is.

options.text: Enable extended thinking so the model reasons more carefully about potential issues in its own code
options.explanation: Extended thinking does not solve the self-review limitation. The model still retains its reasoning context and is biased towards its own output. Extended thinking makes the existing reasoning deeper, not more independent.

options.text: Route the review to a separate Claude instance that has no access to the generation conversation
options.explanation: A model reviewing its own output in the same session retains reasoning context and is less likely to question its own decisions. An independent instance without prior context catches more subtle issues because it approaches the code fresh.

options.text: Lower the temperature during the review phase to make the model more precise and less likely to approve questionable code
options.explanation: Temperature affects response variability, not the fundamental bias of self-review. The model will still be biased towards its own output regardless of temperature settings. An independent instance is the correct architectural fix.

questions.rationale: A model reviewing its own output in the same session retains reasoning context and is less likely to question its own decisions. An independent instance without prior context catches more subtle issues because it approaches the code fresh.

sources.label: Lesson 4.6: Multi-Instance Review and Output Validation (Self-review limitation)

questions.stem: A documentation team wants to archive the full conversation transcript to a log file every time Claude Code runs /compact, so that context lost during compaction can be reviewed later. Which hook configuration achieves this?

options.text: A PostToolUse hook on Write that snapshots the transcript whenever a file is written, on the assumption /compact will eventually run
options.explanation: Write and compaction are unrelated. PostToolUse on Write would fire on every file write whether or not /compact is about to run, producing noise rather than a transcript at the right moment. The dedicated PreCompact event is the correct hook.

options.text: A PreCompact hook that writes the current transcript to a timestamped log file before /compact summarises the conversation
options.explanation: PreCompact is a first-class hook event in Claude Code that fires immediately before /compact (or auto-compaction) runs. The hook receives the full pre-compaction transcript path and can copy or process it before summarisation discards detail.

options.text: A PreToolUse hook configured on a built-in 'Compact' tool, matching tool name 'Compact'
options.explanation: There is no 'Compact' tool exposed to PreToolUse. Compaction is a Claude Code lifecycle operation, not a model-invoked tool, so it has its own dedicated PreCompact event.

options.text: A PostToolUse hook on all tools that appends each tool result to a running log file, creating a continuous archive
options.explanation: Logging every tool result creates enormous log files and does not capture conversation context (reasoning, planning, user messages). The targeted PreCompact event captures the full transcript at the critical moment without per-tool noise.

questions.rationale: PreCompact is a first-class hook event in Claude Code that fires immediately before /compact (or auto-compaction) runs and receives the full pre-compaction transcript path.

questions.stem: A developer productivity platform uses an automated documentation agent. The agent must always extract metadata from source files before generating documentation, but in testing it sometimes skips the metadata extraction step and produces documentation from incomplete information. What is the correct tool_choice configuration to enforce the mandatory first step?

options.text: Set tool_choice to 'auto' and add a system prompt instruction: 'You must call extract_metadata before any other tool.'
options.explanation: With 'auto', the model decides whether to call a tool at all. A system prompt instruction is advisory, not enforced — the model can still skip the step.

options.text: Set tool_choice to 'any' so the model must call a tool, relying on the tool description to guide it to extract_metadata first.
options.explanation: 'any' forces the model to call a tool but lets it choose which one. It may select a different tool first, still skipping extract_metadata.

options.text: Set tool_choice to forced selection with the specific tool name extract_metadata for the first turn, then switch to 'auto' for subsequent turns.
options.explanation: Forced selection {'type': 'tool', 'name': 'extract_metadata'} ensures the model must call this specific tool. After the first turn completes, switching to 'auto' allows normal operation.

options.text: Remove all other tools except extract_metadata from the agent's configuration so it has no choice.
options.explanation: This prevents the agent from performing any other task after metadata extraction. Forced tool selection achieves the constraint without crippling the agent.

questions.rationale: Forced selection guarantees the specific tool is called; switching to 'auto' afterwards restores normal operation.

sources.label: Lesson 2.3: Tool Distribution and Tool Choice

questions.stem: A fintech company requires that all API response payloads are normalised to snake_case before being logged, and that any file write to the src/api/ directory is automatically linted. They want these enforcements to be deterministic and not rely on the model remembering instructions. Which hook configuration achieves both requirements?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook on file writes that runs the linter before the write completes, and a PostToolUse hook on API response handling that normalises field names to snake_case
options.explanation: PreToolUse fires before the tool runs, so there is no file content to lint yet. Linting must happen after the file is written (PostToolUse).

options.text: A PostToolUse hook on file writes to src/api/ that runs the linter on the created file, and a PostToolUse hook on data processing that normalises response payloads to snake_case
options.explanation: Both are PostToolUse hooks because both act on completed outputs. Both provide deterministic enforcement independent of model instructions.

options.text: Add both requirements to CLAUDE.md with clear examples, and add a PreToolUse hook that reminds the model about these rules before each tool call
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md instructions and PreToolUse reminders both rely on the model's compliance, which is not deterministic.

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that blocks any file write to src/api/ unless the file has already been linted, and a PreToolUse hook that blocks API calls unless snake_case normalisation is configured
options.explanation: PreToolUse blocking assumes the file exists before the write, which is contradictory. You cannot lint a file that has not been written yet.

questions.rationale: Both son PostToolUse porque ambos actúan sobre salidas ya completadas, con enforcement determinista.

questions.stem: A legal document extraction pipeline has been running for three months with calibrated confidence thresholds. Extractions above 90% confidence are auto-approved without human review, saving 60% of reviewer time. A new client submits contracts written in an unusual two-column legal format the system has not encountered before. The system reports 92% confidence on these extractions. What is the appropriate safeguard?

options.text: Maintain stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions across document types to catch the new format's error rate.
options.explanation: Stratified random sampling is designed precisely for this scenario: detecting novel error patterns in high-confidence extractions that slip past threshold-based routing.

options.text: Trust the calibrated confidence threshold since it was validated against labelled data and the system reports 92% confidence, which exceeds the 90% auto-approval threshold
options.explanation: Confidence calibration is only valid for document types represented in the calibration data. A novel format can produce miscalibrated confidence scores.

options.text: Raise the confidence threshold from 90% to 98% for all document types to account for novel formats
options.explanation: Raising the threshold globally penalises well-understood document types that are genuinely accurate at 90%+, while still not guaranteeing detection of format-specific issues.

options.text: Add a document format classifier that flags unknown formats for mandatory human review before any auto-approval
options.explanation: While not wrong in principle, this adds ML infrastructure complexity that stratified sampling already handles.

questions.rationale: El muestreo aleatorio estratificado detecta patrones de error nuevos en extracciones de alta confianza que el umbral no filtra.

sources.label: Lesson 5.5: Human Review and Confidence Calibration (Stratified sampling)

questions.discardReason: Rechaza el clasificador de formato porque 'añade complejidad'. Eso es una preferencia de ingeniería, no un principio: un clasificador que marca formatos desconocidos es una respuesta legítima al problema planteado.

questions.stem: A code review agent processes 14 files and produces detailed feedback for the first 5 files but misses obvious bugs in files 10-14. It also flags a pattern as problematic in one file while approving identical code in another. What is the root cause and solution?

options.text: The model's context window is too small — upgrade to a model with a larger context window
options.explanation: Context window size is not the issue. Attention dilution occurs because processing too many items in a single pass produces inconsistent depth, regardless of window size.

options.text: Split the review into per-file local analysis passes plus a separate cross-file integration pass
options.explanation: Multi-pass architecture solves attention dilution. Per-file passes ensure consistent depth for each file. The cross-file integration pass catches data flow issues and ensures consistent pattern evaluation.

options.text: Add a stronger system prompt emphasising the importance of reviewing all files equally
options.explanation: Prompt improvements do not solve attention dilution. It is an architectural problem requiring a structural solution.

options.text: Reduce the number of files reviewed per run to 5 and process in batches
options.explanation: Batching is closer to the right idea but misses the cross-file integration pass, so cross-file data flow issues and pattern consistency are not addressed.

questions.rationale: La arquitectura multi-pase resuelve la dilución de atención: pases por archivo más un pase de integración cruzada.

questions.stem: Your extraction pipeline reports 97% aggregate accuracy, and you want to automate high-confidence extractions. Which safeguards should be in place before you reduce human review? (Select 3)

options.text: Calibrate field-level confidence thresholds against a labelled validation set.
options.explanation: Confidence scores only route review attention correctly once they are calibrated on labelled data.

options.text: Rely on the aggregate accuracy figure once it has held steady for a full quarter.
options.explanation: Stability of the aggregate number does not reveal per-segment weaknesses.

options.text: Verify accuracy separately by document type and field segment, not just in aggregate.
options.explanation: A strong aggregate figure can mask poor performance on specific document types or fields.

options.text: Keep stratified random samples of high-confidence extractions under review to measure error rates and catch novel patterns.
options.explanation: Stratified sampling is el mecanismo de medición continua tras automatizar.

options.text: Expand the review team until every extraction can be checked by hand.
options.explanation: Reviewing everything ignores the point of calibration: routing limited reviewer capacity to low-confidence and ambiguous cases.

questions.rationale: Antes de automatizar hacen falta validación por segmento, confianza calibrada por campo y muestreo estratificado continuo.

sources.label: Lesson 5.5: Human Review and Confidence Calibration

questions.stem: Your extraction pipeline correctly identifies data in structured tables but returns empty fields when the same information appears in narrative paragraphs. Detailed instructions specify all required fields. What should you try first?

options.text: Increase the model's context window to process more of the document
options.explanation: The model already finds data in tables. The issue is not context size but inconsistent handling of different document structures.

options.text: Add few-shot examples showing correct extraction from both structured tables and narrative paragraphs
options.explanation: Few-shot examples demonstrating correct handling of varied document structures directly address inconsistent extraction quality across formats.

options.text: Add a pre-processing step to convert all narrative text into tables
options.explanation: This adds unnecessary complexity. The model should handle varied formats — few-shot examples teach it how.

options.text: Add a post-processing retry that re-extracts any empty fields
options.explanation: Retrying without better guidance will produce the same empty results.

questions.rationale: Ejemplos few-shot que cubren estructuras variadas atacan directamente la inconsistencia entre formatos.

questions.stem: The moderation system handles appeals where users contest a moderation decision. Currently, the same agent that made the original decision re-evaluates the appeal. Appeal overturn rates are suspiciously low. What is the most effective architectural change?

options.text: Add stronger instructions to the appeal handler's prompt requiring it to weigh the user's perspective fairly and set aside its earlier decision.
options.explanation: Prompt instructions cannot overcome the bias of an agent reviewing its own decision.

options.text: Route every appeal to a human reviewer with full authority to overturn the automated decision, taking the original agent out of the appeal path entirely.
options.explanation: Human review for every appeal does not scale and removes the benefit of automated moderation.

options.text: Route appeals to a separate agent instance that cannot see the original reasoning, given only the content and the user's justification.
options.explanation: A fresh agent instance without access to the original reasoning context evaluates the content independently, avoiding confirmation bias.

options.text: Automatically overturn decisions where the user provides any appeal justification to improve user trust
options.explanation: Automatic overturn on any appeal completely undermines moderation.

questions.rationale: Una instancia nueva sin acceso al razonamiento original evalúa de forma independiente y evita el sesgo de confirmación.

sources.label: Lesson 1.7: Session State and Resumption (Stale context)

questions.stem: A team wants to enforce that all SQL migration files created by Claude Code follow a strict naming convention (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_description.sql) and contain a rollback section. Which approach provides deterministic enforcement without relying on the model's judgment?

options.text: Add a PostToolUse hook on file creation that validates the filename pattern and checks for a rollback section
options.explanation: PostToolUse hooks run deterministic validation code after tool execution, providing reliable automated enforcement.

options.text: Document the naming convention and rollback requirement in the project CLAUDE.md with clear examples
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md instructions rely on the model's interpretation and compliance.

options.text: Create a .claude/rules/migrations.md file with paths: ["**/migrations/**/*.sql"] containing the naming convention
options.explanation: Rules files provide context-specific instructions but still rely on the model to follow them.

options.text: Use a PreToolUse hook to inject the naming convention into every prompt before file creation occurs
options.explanation: Injecting instructions into prompts still relies on the model's compliance. PostToolUse validation checks the actual output.

questions.rationale: Los hooks PostToolUse ejecutan código de validación determinista después de la herramienta.

questions.stem: A tool returns an empty array after a customer lookup. The agent retries 3 times, then escalates to a human agent. Analysis shows the customer's account simply does not exist. What is the root cause of this wasted effort?

options.text: The retry limit is too low — increasing to 5 retries would resolve the issue.
options.explanation: More retries make the problem worse. The tool succeeded — it found no matching customer.

options.text: The tool does not distinguish between access failures and valid empty results, so the agent treats 'no matches' as a retriable failure.
options.explanation: The tool successfully queried the data source and found no matches. This is a valid empty result, not an access failure.

options.text: The escalation threshold is too aggressive — the agent should exhaust more retries before involving a human.
options.explanation: The problem is not the escalation threshold; it is that the agent retries at all.

options.text: The system prompt should instruct the agent not to retry customer lookups.
options.explanation: Hard-coding retry rules per tool in the system prompt is brittle. The proper fix is structured error metadata.

questions.rationale: Un resultado vacío válido no es un fallo de acceso; conflatearlos provoca reintentos y escalados innecesarios.

sources.label: Lesson 2.2: Structured Error Responses (Access failure vs empty result)

questions.stem: A documentation generation pipeline uses Claude Code to produce docs from three sources: source code comments, existing wiki pages, and API schema files. During a run, the wiki page retrieval fails with a timeout, but the source code and API schema are available. The pipeline currently halts entirely on any source failure. What is the best error handling strategy?

options.text: Retry the wiki retrieval three times with exponential backoff. If all retries fail, halt the pipeline to prevent incomplete documentation
options.explanation: Halting the entire pipeline because one of three sources is unavailable wastes the successful results from the other two.

options.text: Return structured error context for the wiki failure, proceed with available sources, and mark the gaps that lack wiki content.
options.explanation: Produces maximum value from available sources while maintaining transparency about what is missing.

options.text: Silently skip the wiki source and generate documentation from the remaining two sources without noting the omission
options.explanation: Silent omission hides the failure; users would trust the documentation as complete.

options.text: Use the source code comments to infer what the wiki pages would have contained, filling in the gaps with generated content
options.explanation: Inferring wiki content from source code produces hallucinated documentation that appears authoritative.

questions.rationale: Contexto de error estructurado + continuar con lo disponible + anotar los huecos de cobertura.

sources.label: Lesson 5.3: Error Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems

questions.stem: A customer support agent has two tools: get_customer_profile (returns name, email, preferences) and get_customer_orders (returns order history with statuses). Users frequently ask 'Tell me about customer X', and the agent calls both tools sequentially, doubling response time. 90% of 'tell me about' queries only need the profile. What is the best approach?

options.text: Consolidate both tools into a single get_customer_info tool that returns all customer data in one call.
options.explanation: Consolidation returns order data on every call, wasting resources for the 90% of queries that only need profile data.

options.text: Refine the descriptions so get_customer_profile is the default and get_customer_orders is order-specific.
options.explanation: Refining tool descriptions with clear defaults is the lowest-effort fix and directs the agent to call only the profile tool unless order details are explicitly requested.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction: 'When a user says tell me about, only call get_customer_profile.'
options.explanation: Hard-coding keyword-to-tool mappings in the system prompt is brittle and does not generalise to other phrasings.

options.text: Set tool_choice to forced selection of get_customer_profile for all turns to prevent unnecessary order lookups.
options.explanation: Forced selection prevents the agent from ever calling get_customer_orders, even when users specifically ask about orders.

questions.rationale: Las descripciones de herramientas con límites claros y routing por defecto son el arreglo estructural de menor costo.

questions.stem: An invoice-extraction pipeline mislabels fields on documents where the correct interpretation is ambiguous. Which few-shot practices should you apply? (Select 2)

options.text: Add an example for every document variant seen in production so far.
options.explanation: Volume is not the fix; a handful of targeted examples beats exhaustive coverage and its context cost.

options.text: Use examples showing correct extraction from varied document structures to fix empty or null extraction of required fields.
options.explanation: Varied-structure examples fix empty or null extraction of fields that are present; fabrication of absent data se maneja con campos nullable.

options.text: Replace the examples with a longer natural-language description of each field.
options.explanation: Las descripciones solas son lo que produjo la inconsistencia.

options.text: Create two to four targeted examples for the ambiguous cases, showing why one interpretation is chosen.
options.explanation: Ejemplos dirigidos que demuestran el razonamiento son el remedio específico para casos ambiguos.

questions.rationale: Para casos ambiguos: pocos ejemplos dirigidos con razonamiento, más cobertura de estructuras variadas.

questions.stem: A coordinator delegates to a data collection agent (web_search, database_query) and an analysis agent (calculate, chart_generate). In testing, the analysis agent calls web_search directly to fetch extra context, bypassing the data collection agent. What is the architectural violation and how should it be fixed?

options.text: The analysis agent's allowedTools includes web_search; remove it so only the data collection agent has it.
options.explanation: Each agent should only have tools relevant to its specific role. If the analysis agent needs more data, it should request it through the coordinator.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the analysis agent not to use web_search even though it has access
options.explanation: Prompt instructions are probabilistic. The fix is to remove the tool from allowedTools.

options.text: Allow the analysis agent to keep web_search access since it sometimes needs additional context for better analysis
options.explanation: This violates scoped tool access and bypasses the data collection agent's role.

options.text: Implement a PostToolUse hook that logs when the analysis agent uses web_search for monitoring purposes
options.explanation: Logging the violation does not prevent it.

questions.rationale: Acceso a herramientas por rol: quitar la herramienta de allowedTools es el arreglo determinista.

questions.stem: A developer needs to find all files that call a deprecated function processLegacyOrder() and also find all test files for those callers. Which tool sequence is correct?

options.text: Glob for '*processLegacyOrder*' to find the callers, then Grep the results for the matching test files.
options.explanation: Glob matches file paths, not file contents. It cannot find function callers.

options.text: Read every source file to search for the function calls, then Read every test file to confirm the callers.
options.explanation: Reading all files upfront is a context-budget killer.

options.text: Grep for 'processLegacyOrder' to find the callers, then Glob to match their test files by name.
options.explanation: Grep searches file contents (correcto para encontrar llamadas); Glob matches file paths (correcto para archivos de test por patrón).

options.text: Bash with 'find . -name "*.ts" | xargs grep processLegacyOrder' for the callers and again for the tests.
options.explanation: Aunque funciona, evita las herramientas nativas diseñadas para estas tareas.

questions.rationale: Grep busca CONTENIDO, Glob busca RUTAS. Esa es la distinción central.

questions.stem: A consulting firm's multi-agent research system has a coordinator that always invokes the full pipeline of five subagents (web search, document analysis, data extraction, synthesis, and formatting) for every query, including simple factual lookups that only need web search. This adds unnecessary latency and cost. What is the correct architectural fix?

options.text: Have the coordinator select which subagents to invoke per query, not always the full pipeline.
options.explanation: El coordinador debe analizar los requisitos de la consulta y decidir qué subagentes hacen falta. La selección dinámica reduce latencia y costo.

options.text: Allow subagents to communicate directly with each other so they can skip unnecessary steps in the pipeline
options.explanation: Direct subagent communication violates the hub-and-spoke architecture.

options.text: Add a caching layer in front of the pipeline so subagents with no work to do return a cached empty result immediately.
options.explanation: Invocar subagentes innecesarios añade overhead de llamadas y latencia aunque los resultados estén cacheados.

options.text: Split into two separate systems: one for simple queries and one for complex queries
options.explanation: Mantener dos sistemas separados crea complejidad innecesaria; el coordinador ya existe para enrutar.

questions.rationale: Selección dinámica de subagentes según los requisitos de cada consulta.

questions.stem: A docs team processes a 500,000-line codebase by having Claude Code read files and generate docs, instructing it to 'summarise each module after documenting it, then discard the detailed source from context.' After processing 20 modules, the docs for module 21 reference class names from module 3 that were renamed in module 12. What caused this failure?

options.text: Progressive summarisation lost the rename detail: when module 12's summary replaced its source code, the rename was condensed to 'various refactoring changes', so the agent retained module 3's original class names from its earlier summary
options.explanation: El resumen progresivo es con pérdida. Los cambios críticos entre módulos (como renombrados) deben vivir en un bloque de hechos persistente fuera del contexto resumido.

options.text: The agent's context window overflowed, causing it to hallucinate class names from earlier modules
options.explanation: El equipo gestiona el contexto resumiendo y descartando fuente, así que no hay desbordamiento. El problema es la calidad de lo retenido.

options.text: Claude Code cached module 3's source code and served the stale version instead of the updated file on disk
options.explanation: Claude Code no cachea contenidos de archivo entre lecturas; cada Read trae el archivo actual del disco.

options.text: The model confused similar class names because it processed too many modules in a single session
options.explanation: No es confusión genérica: es consecuencia directa de perder el detalle del renombrado durante el resumen progresivo.

questions.rationale: El resumen progresivo pierde detalles; los cambios cruzados entre módulos deben registrarse en un bloque de hechos persistente.

questions.stem: A multi-agent research system produces a report on 'renewable energy technologies' that only covers solar and wind, missing geothermal, tidal, biomass, and nuclear fusion. Each subagent produced thorough coverage of its assigned topic. Where is the root cause?

options.text: The web search subagent scoped its queries too narrowly, so geothermal, tidal, biomass and fusion never surfaced in the results it returned.
options.explanation: El subagente investigó lo que se le asignó y devolvió cobertura completa de esa asignación.

options.text: The synthesis subagent failed to audit its inputs for coverage gaps, so it wrote up solar and wind as though they were the whole field.
options.explanation: El agente de síntesis solo puede trabajar con la investigación que recibe.

options.text: The coordinator's task decomposition assigned only solar and wind, omitting the other renewable categories.
options.explanation: El coordinador es responsable de descomponer el tema amplio en subtemas. Si solo asigna solar y eólica, ningún agente aguas abajo puede cubrir el resto.

options.text: The document analysis subagent lacked access to sources on geothermal, tidal, biomass, and fusion, so those categories never entered the report.
options.explanation: La disponibilidad de fuentes no es la causa raíz: nadie recibió el encargo de investigarlas.

questions.rationale: Rastrea los fallos hasta su origen: la descomposición del coordinador.

questions.stem: Your CI/CD pipeline processes code reviews using the Message Batches API. After a batch completes, you need to match each review result back to the corresponding pull request. What is the correct mechanism for correlating batch results with their original requests?

options.text: Parse the review content to identify which pull request it refers to based on file names mentioned in the review
options.explanation: El parseo de contenido es frágil; la API ya ofrece un mecanismo integrado.

options.text: Rely on the batch API returning results in the same order they were submitted
options.explanation: Los resultados del batch no garantizan el orden de envío.

options.text: Use the custom_id field in each batch request to store the pull request identifier, then match results by custom_id
options.explanation: El campo custom_id existe justamente para correlacionar pares request/response de un batch.

options.text: Submit each pull request as a separate batch of one item to maintain correlation through the batch ID
options.explanation: Anula el propósito del procesamiento por lotes.

questions.rationale: custom_id es el mecanismo de correlación del Batch API.

sources.label: Lesson 4.5: Batch Processing and Prompt Optimisation (custom_id matching)

questions.stem: A team's agent must generate a weekly report on the first turn of each conversation by calling generate_report. With tool_choice: 'auto', the agent sometimes responds with a text summary instead. The team wants to guarantee generate_report is called on turn one while allowing normal tool selection afterwards. What is the correct configuration?

options.text: Set tool_choice to 'any' on every turn of the conversation, so the agent is always obliged to call one of its available tools.
options.explanation: 'any' fuerza una llamada pero no cuál, y además impide respuestas de texto normales en los turnos siguientes.

options.text: Set tool_choice to forced selection of generate_report for the first turn, then switch to 'auto' for subsequent turns.
options.explanation: La selección forzada con nombre garantiza la llamada en el primer turno; 'auto' después restaura el comportamiento normal.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction stating 'Always call generate_report on the first turn' and leave tool_choice on 'auto'.
options.explanation: Las instrucciones del system prompt son orientativas, no forzosas.

options.text: Remove all other tools except generate_report from the first turn's tool list, then add the remaining tools for subsequent turns.
options.explanation: Funcionaría, pero modificar dinámicamente la lista de herramientas es innecesariamente complejo.

questions.rationale: Forzado en turno 1 y 'auto' después.

sources.label: Lesson 2.3: Tool Distribution and Tool Choice (Forced tool selection)

questions.stem: A research coordinator spawns 4 subagents to investigate different aspects of a market analysis. Agent A fails with an API error, Agent B returns partial results (3 of 5 requested data points), and Agents C and D return complete results. The final report is due in 2 hours. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Retry Agent A, discard Agent B's partial results as unreliable, and wait for both agents to return fully complete data before writing the report.
options.explanation: Descartar los resultados parciales de B desperdicia datos válidos y esperar ignora el plazo.

options.text: Proceed with only Agents C and D's results and produce the report without the data from Agents A and B
options.explanation: Descarta innecesariamente los resultados parciales de B y abandona el alcance de A.

options.text: Retry Agent A, incorporate Agent B's partial results, flag B's missing data points as gaps, and synthesise from all available results.
options.explanation: Maximiza el uso de datos: reintentar el fallo, incorporar lo parcial marcando los huecos y sintetizar todo lo disponible.

options.text: Terminate all agents and restart the entire investigation from scratch with a simplified scope
options.explanation: Reiniciar descarta los resultados completos de C y D.

questions.rationale: Maximizar utilización de datos con anotaciones explícitas de huecos.
questions.discardReason: Con plazo de 2 horas, 'seguir solo con C y D' es una decisión defendible. La clave asume que siempre hay margen para reintentar.

questions.stem: A documentation team must update architecture guides across 25 microservice directories after a platform migration. Each guide requires reading source, checking dependencies, and rewriting affected sections. Working in direct execution mode, a team member updates three services before noticing the results are inconsistent: some guides still mention the old platform, others use inconsistent terminology for the new one. What went wrong and what is the correct approach?

options.text: The team member should have used plan mode to set a consistent update strategy and terminology before executing across all 25 services
options.explanation: Plan mode produce una estrategia explícita de terminología, orden y criterios de validación antes de tocar nada.

options.text: Direct execution was correct but should have been done in a single continuous session to maintain consistency through conversation context
options.explanation: Una sola sesión con 25 servicios agotaría la ventana de contexto y empeoraría la inconsistencia.

options.text: The team member should have created a custom slash command that hardcodes the exact text replacements for each service
options.explanation: Las guías de arquitectura requieren comprensión contextual, no reemplazo mecánico de texto.

options.text: The team member should have used the Explore subagent to discover all affected files first, then made all changes in a single batch
options.explanation: El descubrimiento por sí solo no resuelve la consistencia.

questions.rationale: Cambios multi-archivo con requisitos de consistencia piden planificación explícita antes de escribir.

sources.label: Lesson 3.4: Plan Mode vs Direct Execution

questions.stem: Your federated query platform exposes several similar search tools, and Claude keeps routing requests to the wrong one. Which changes improve tool selection reliability? (Select 3)

options.text: Rename tools whose names overlap so each name reflects a distinct function.
options.explanation: Renombrar elimina el solapamiento funcional que causa el misrouting.

options.text: Trim every description to one short sentence so the model relies on tool names alone.
options.explanation: Las descripciones mínimas provocan selección poco fiable entre herramientas similares.

options.text: Check the system prompt for keyword-sensitive instructions that create unintended associations with particular tools.
options.explanation: El wording del system prompt puede sobrescribir descripciones bien escritas.

options.text: Rewrite each description to state the tool's purpose, inputs and outputs, and when to prefer it.
options.explanation: Las descripciones son la señal principal de selección.

options.text: Merge the similar tools into one generic tool with a mode parameter.
options.explanation: La guía va en dirección contraria: dividir herramientas genéricas en específicas con contratos definidos.

questions.rationale: Descripciones diferenciadas, nombres distintos y un system prompt que no pelee con las definiciones.

questions.stem: A developer's customer support agent sometimes terminates prematurely because they check if response.content[0].type == 'text' to determine completion. The agent stops even when Claude has more tools to call. What is the bug and how should they fix it?

options.text: Add an iteration cap of 15 loops and treat reaching the cap as the signal that the agent has finished its work.
options.explanation: Los topes arbitrarios no atacan la causa y usarlos como señal de finalización es en sí un anti-patrón.

options.text: Check the stop_reason field instead of content type: continue on 'tool_use', terminate on 'end_turn'.
options.explanation: stop_reason es la señal determinista y autoritativa para el control del bucle. Claude puede devolver texto junto a bloques tool_use.

options.text: Parse the assistant's text for completion phrases like 'I have completed' and treat the first match as the signal to stop.
options.explanation: El parseo de lenguaje natural es ambiguo y poco fiable.

options.text: Set tool_choice to 'any' so Claude always calls a tool instead of returning text
options.explanation: Fuerza uso de herramientas incluso cuando el agente ya terminó, creando un bucle infinito.

questions.rationale: stop_reason == 'tool_use' continúa; 'end_turn' termina.

questions.stem: An extraction pipeline processes 50-page legal contracts in a single API call. It captures parties and dates from the first few pages but misses key financial terms in later pages, and occasionally contradicts itself across fields. A colleague suggests simply increasing the context window. What is the correct diagnosis and fix?

options.text: The context window is too small; upgrading to a larger context model will fix the inconsistency
options.explanation: Si el documento cabe en la ventana, agrandarla no mejora la calidad de la atención.

options.text: This is attention dilution; split into per-section extraction passes plus a cross-section reconciliation pass.
options.explanation: Los pases por sección garantizan atención dedicada y el pase de integración reconcilia contradicciones.

options.text: Run the full extraction three times and take the most common value for each field
options.explanation: Varios pases sobre el documento completo sufren la misma dilución de atención.

options.text: Add more detailed instructions about the importance of financial terms to increase the model's focus on those sections
options.explanation: Las instrucciones no pueden vencer la dilución de atención en un documento de 50 páginas.

questions.rationale: Dilución de atención: pases por sección más reconciliación cruzada.

sources.label: Lesson 4.6: Multi-Instance Review and Output Validation

questions.stem: A CI/CD pipeline runs three Claude Code steps in sequence: (1) generate a changelog from git commits, (2) review the changelog for accuracy, and (3) check for breaking changes. The team notices that step 2 never flags inaccuracies and step 3 misses obvious breaking changes that the changelog omits. What is the root cause?

options.text: The three steps share session context, so steps 2 and 3 inherit step 1's reasoning instead of judging the changelog
options.explanation: Cuando los pasos de revisión comparten contexto con el de generación, heredan el razonamiento original. El aislamiento de sesión es crítico en pipelines de revisión.

options.text: The CLAUDE.md file does not contain changelog formatting standards, so the review step has no criteria to evaluate against
options.explanation: La falta de estándares afectaría la calidad del changelog generado, no la capacidad de la revisión de detectar imprecisiones.

options.text: The -p flag is not being used, causing each step to wait for interactive input
options.explanation: Sin -p el pipeline se colgaría, no produciría salida que omite problemas.

options.text: The steps need to use --output-format json so that each step can parse the previous step's structured output
options.explanation: El formato de salida no determina si la revisión es exhaustiva.

questions.rationale: Aislamiento de contexto de sesión entre generación y revisión.

questions.stem: Your extraction pipeline has a validation step that checks extracted financial data. When validation fails, the system retries by sending just the original document with the same prompt. Retry success rates are below 10%. The most common failure is the model placing the 'net amount' value in the 'gross amount' field and vice versa. How should the retry be restructured?

options.text: Increase retries from 1 to 5, since more attempts at the same prompt will eventually produce the correct field mapping by chance
options.explanation: Si el modelo mapea mal de forma consistente, más reintentos sin feedback producen el mismo error.

options.text: Send the original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation error naming the swapped fields.
options.explanation: El retry-with-error-feedback es mucho más efectivo: ver el error específico permite autocorrección dirigida.

options.text: Add a post-processing rule that automatically swaps net and gross amounts when validation detects the pattern
options.explanation: Las reglas de intercambio hardcodeadas son frágiles y ocultan el error de extracción subyacente.

options.text: Switch to a different model for the retry, since the original model has a persistent field-mapping bias
options.explanation: El problema es la ausencia de contexto de error en el reintento, no el modelo.

questions.rationale: Reintento con feedback del error específico, no reintento ciego.

sources.label: Lesson 4.4: Validation, Retry, and Feedback Loops

questions.stem: A web search agent has 9 tools: web_search, url_fetch, html_parse, pdf_extract, image_ocr, translate, summarise, keyword_extract, sentiment_analysis. In testing it frequently calls summarise and sentiment_analysis when it should only fetch raw data. How should the architect fix this?

options.text: Add system prompt instructions telling the web search agent to only use data fetching tools and ignore analysis tools
options.explanation: Las instrucciones son probabilísticas y el agente ya está haciendo mal uso.

options.text: Reduce the web search agent to the 4-5 data-fetching tools and move the analysis tools to the specialist agents.
options.explanation: El máximo recomendado es 4-5 herramientas por agente. Las de análisis pertenecen a los agentes de síntesis o análisis.

options.text: Keep all 9 tools but implement PreToolUse hooks that block the web search agent from calling summarise and sentiment_analysis
options.explanation: Usar hooks para bloquear acceso es una solución sobre-ingenierizada a lo que es un arreglo de configuración.

options.text: Merge the web search and synthesis agents into a single agent since they share some tools
options.explanation: Fusionar agentes viola el principio de subagentes especializados y agranda el set de herramientas.

questions.rationale: 4-5 herramientas por agente y alcance por rol.

sources.label: Lesson 1.4: Workflow Enforcement and Handoff (Scoped tool access)

questions.stem: A validation-retry loop still fails on the same documents after three attempts each. In which situations will further retries not help? (Select 2)

options.text: The model placed a correct value in the wrong field on the last attempt.
options.explanation: Es un error semántico de validación; el retry con feedback nombrando el campo mal ubicado guía la corrección.

options.text: The required information is simply absent from the source document.
options.explanation: Ningún reintento hace aparecer información inexistente.

options.text: The validation service timed out on the last attempt.
options.explanation: Un timeout es un fallo transitorio, justo la clase de error que un reintento resuelve.

options.text: The information exists only in an external document that is not provided in context.
options.explanation: Los reintentos no alcanzan datos fuera del contexto del modelo.

questions.rationale: Los reintentos sirven ante fallos transitorios o corregibles con feedback, no ante información ausente o fuera de contexto.

sources.label: Lesson 4.4: Validation, Retry, and Feedback Loops (Retry boundary)

questions.stem: A team wants their CI pipeline to run Claude Code for both PR code review and automated test generation. The PR review should output structured JSON for integration with their review dashboard, while the test generation should produce standard text output. How should the two pipeline steps be configured?

options.text: Run both steps with -p and configure the review dashboard to parse plain text output from both steps
options.explanation: El texto plano exige lógica de parseo frágil en el dashboard.

options.text: Run the review step with -p --output-format json and the test generation step with -p only, as separate non-interactive invocations
options.explanation: Cada paso usa -p; solo el de revisión añade --output-format json. Invocaciones separadas garantizan aislamiento de sesión.

options.text: Run both steps in a single Claude Code session with -p, using different prompts to request different output formats
options.explanation: Una sola sesión viola el aislamiento de contexto entre generación y revisión.

options.text: Run both steps with --output-format json and have the test generation step extract code from the JSON response
options.explanation: Añade complejidad innecesaria al paso de generación de tests.

questions.rationale: -p en ambos, JSON solo donde hace falta parseo, e invocaciones independientes.

questions.stem: A research subagent's database query fails partway through an investigation. Which pieces of information belong in the structured error context it returns to the coordinator? (Select 3)

options.text: No report at all: the subagent should retry silently until the query succeeds.
options.explanation: Los reintentos silenciosos ocultan fallos al coordinador, que es quien gestiona los errores.

options.text: Partial results gathered before the failure.
options.explanation: Preservan el trabajo ya completado y evitan repetirlo.

options.text: The failure type, such as transient, validation, or permission.
options.explanation: Categorizar el fallo permite decidir entre reintentar o redirigir.

options.text: What was attempted, including the query that failed.
options.explanation: Da al coordinador detalle suficiente para reintentar de forma inteligente o reformular.

options.text: A plain 'no results found' message in place of the error.
options.explanation: Reportar un fallo de acceso como resultado vacío confunde dos situaciones distintas.

questions.rationale: Tipo de fallo, qué se intentó y resultados parciales.

questions.stem: The pipeline validates each tool_use extraction against a Pydantic model with model_validate(). Validation succeeds and every field has the correct type, yet extracted totals still disagree with the documents' stated totals. What explains this, and what is the fix?

options.text: model_validate() is failing silently; pin an older Pydantic version until the regression is fixed
options.explanation: model_validate() hizo su trabajo: la extracción cumple los tipos del modelo. La comprobación faltante nunca se definió.

options.text: Type checks passed but no rule relates the totals; add a model validator for the sum rule and route its errors into retries
options.explanation: Conformidad de esquema y corrección semántica son capas distintas; la relación de suma debe escribirse como validador.

options.text: The schema needs numeric minimum and maximum constraints on the stated_total field so that mismatched totals are rejected at parse time
options.explanation: Un rango por campo no puede expresar una relación entre dos campos.

options.text: Semantic disagreement indicates hallucination; lower the temperature so extraction becomes deterministic
options.explanation: El determinismo solo repetiría la misma extracción incorrecta.

questions.rationale: Validación de esquema ≠ validación semántica; la regla de suma va en código de validación y su error alimenta el reintento.
questions.conflictNote: Mismo síntoma que EX-003: la guía propone calculated_total vs stated_total con revisión humana.

sources.label: Lesson 4.4: Validation, Retry, and Feedback Loops (Pydantic as the validation layer)

questions.stem: A CI pipeline validates that generated API docs match the codebase. It runs claude -p 'Verify that all public API endpoints in src/api/ have corresponding documentation in docs/api/' with --output-format json. The check consistently reports 100% coverage, yet manual audits regularly find undocumented endpoints. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The --output-format json flag corrupts the analysis results, causing false positives
options.explanation: --output-format json controla la estructura de salida, no la lógica de análisis.

options.text: Claude Code is doing a shallow pattern match, not a deep semantic comparison, and the prompt lacks validation criteria
options.explanation: Sin criterios de validación explícitos el modelo puede hacer una comprobación superficial. Añadir criterios estructurados y ejemplos de qué cuenta como hueco produce verificación fiable.

options.text: The -p flag prevents Claude Code from reading files, so it generates a plausible-sounding report without actual file access
options.explanation: -p ejecuta en modo no interactivo; no restringe el acceso a archivos.

options.text: The CI pipeline needs a separate review step where a second Claude Code instance verifies the first instance's findings
options.explanation: Una segunda instancia revisando la misma salida vaga llegará a las mismas conclusiones.

questions.rationale: Faltan criterios de validación explícitos en el prompt.

questions.stem: Claude Code is auditing API documentation coverage across a large codebase. After exploring 15 modules, the agent produces vague references like 'the authentication module follows standard patterns' instead of citing specific class names and method signatures it discovered earlier. /compact has already been used once. What is the most effective next step?

options.text: Run /compact again to further reduce context usage and continue the exploration in the same session.
options.explanation: Compactar de nuevo no restaura los hallazgos específicos ya perdidos.

options.text: Delegate remaining module explorations to subagents, giving each a scratchpad summary of findings so far.
options.explanation: La delegación aísla la salida verbosa del contexto principal y el scratchpad persiste los hallazgos específicos.

options.text: Start a fresh session and re-explore all 15 modules more efficiently to rebuild the context with only essential findings.
options.explanation: Reexplorar 15 módulos desperdicia tiempo y esfuerzo considerables.

options.text: Increase the model's temperature to encourage more detailed and specific outputs instead of vague pattern references.
options.explanation: La temperatura no afecta la capacidad de recordar hallazgos previos.

questions.rationale: Delegación a subagentes + scratchpad persistente.

sources.label: Lesson 5.4: Codebase Exploration and Context Degradation

questions.stem: A CI/CD system prompt defines two review categories with the instructions 'Check for security vulnerabilities in each function' and 'Check for performance issues in each loop'. The model frequently calls performance_check for security issues found inside loops, and security_check for performance issues in security-sensitive functions. What is the root cause and best fix?

options.text: The model is confused because loops can have both security and performance issues; add a rule that security always takes priority over performance
options.explanation: Las reglas de prioridad añaden complejidad sin atacar la causa.

options.text: Keyword overlap between the instruction phrasing and the tool names causes the confusion; rewrite them to use distinct, non-overlapping terms.
options.explanation: Cuando el texto de la instrucción solapa con patrones de nombres de herramientas, el modelo confunde keywords de instrucción con señales de selección.

options.text: Add more detailed tool descriptions explaining exactly when each tool should be called
options.explanation: Ayuda, pero no arregla la causa si el texto de instrucción sigue conteniendo keywords solapadas.

options.text: Force tool_choice to 'auto' and let the model determine the correct tool based on the content of each finding
options.explanation: 'auto' probablemente ya es el ajuste; el problema es el solapamiento de keywords.

questions.rationale: Solapamiento de keywords entre instrucciones y nombres de herramientas.

sources.label: Lesson 4.1: System Prompts with Explicit Criteria

questions.stem: A developer's Claude Code applies the team's API conventions correctly in some sessions but not others, on the same project. They suspect the wrong memory files are loading in the failing sessions. What is the fastest way to confirm which CLAUDE.md and rules files a session has actually loaded?

options.text: Run /memory in the session to list the loaded memory files
options.explanation: /memory es el comando de diagnóstico de la jerarquía: muestra qué archivos de memoria de nivel usuario, proyecto y directorio cargó la sesión.

options.text: Run /compact to reload the configuration hierarchy from disk
options.explanation: /compact resume la conversación; no recarga ni reporta archivos de configuración.

options.text: Delete ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so only project-level configuration can load
options.explanation: Es una suposición destructiva que no confirma nada.

options.text: Ask Claude in the session to repeat the team's API conventions back
options.explanation: El modelo puede parafrasear desde su entrenamiento, así que una respuesta fluida no prueba que los archivos se cargaron.

questions.rationale: /memory inspecciona la jerarquía viva de forma determinista.

questions.stem: A customer support team configures an MCP server for their internal CRM system. The agent frequently ignores the CRM MCP tool and instead uses the built-in Grep tool to search local log files for customer information, producing incomplete results. The MCP tool's description reads: 'CRM tool'. What should the team do first?

options.text: Remove the Grep tool from the agent's available tools so it cannot fall back to local file search.
options.explanation: Quitar Grep inutiliza al agente para búsquedas legítimas. El problema es la descripción, no la existencia de Grep.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction: 'Always use the CRM tool for customer queries. Never use Grep for customer data.'
options.explanation: Hardcodear preferencias en el system prompt es frágil y no escala.

options.text: Move the MCP server configuration from .mcp.json to ~/.claude.json so it takes higher priority.
options.explanation: El ámbito de configuración no afecta la prioridad de selección de herramientas.

options.text: Expand the sparse 'CRM tool' description to detail its full customer records and structured output.
options.explanation: Cuando la descripción de una herramienta MCP es escueta, el agente cae en herramientas nativas familiares. Enriquecerla es el arreglo recomendado para la infrautilización de MCP.

questions.rationale: Descripción MCP enriquecida (registros completos, historial, estado de cuenta, salida estructurada).

questions.stem: Your Claude Code agent generates unit tests in the CI pipeline. When given detailed instructions alone, it produces tests with inconsistent assertion styles: sometimes using expect().toBe(), sometimes assert.equal(), and occasionally mixing both in the same file. Adding more detailed instructions about assertion style did not fix the problem. What should you do next?

options.text: Switch to a different model that better follows formatting instructions
options.explanation: No es un problema de capacidad del modelo.

options.text: Add a linter post-processing step to automatically convert all assertions to a single style
options.explanation: El post-procesado enmascara el problema en vez de resolverlo.

options.text: Add 2-4 few-shot examples showing complete test files with the desired assertion style and reasoning for why that style was chosen over alternatives
options.explanation: Parcialmente correcto pero incompleto: sin cubrir escenarios variados (async, manejo de errores) el modelo hace pattern-matching de los casos mostrados en vez de generalizar.

options.text: Add 2-4 few-shot examples demonstrating the desired assertion style with reasoning for each testing decision, covering edge cases like async functions and error handling
options.explanation: Los ejemplos few-shot son la técnica más efectiva cuando las instrucciones detalladas por sí solas producen formato inconsistente. Incluir razonamiento enseña a generalizar; cubrir escenarios variados asegura la generalización correcta.

questions.rationale: 2-4 ejemplos con razonamiento y cobertura de casos límite. Ojo: C y D son casi idénticas y la diferencia está en la cobertura de edge cases.
questions.discardReason: Las opciones C y D son la misma respuesta (2-4 ejemplos few-shot); D solo añade 'cubriendo casos límite'. C está marcada incorrecta pero no es falsa, solo menos completa.

questions.stem: In a hub-and-spoke research system, a coordinator manages several search and analysis subagents. Which responsibilities sit with the coordinator rather than with individual subagents? (Select 3)

options.text: Sharing its full conversation history with each subagent automatically at spawn time.
options.explanation: Los subagentes corren con contexto aislado; nada se hereda automáticamente.

options.text: Deciding which subagents to invoke based on the complexity of each incoming query.
options.explanation: La selección dinámica de subagentes es del coordinador.

options.text: Routing all inter-agent communication so subagents never exchange messages directly.
options.explanation: Hub-and-spoke enruta todo mensaje por el coordinador para observabilidad y manejo de errores consistente.

options.text: Running every search itself first so subagents only verify its findings.
options.explanation: El coordinador delega en vez de duplicar el trabajo.

options.text: Aggregating subagent results and re-delegating targeted follow-up queries when synthesis shows gaps.
options.explanation: Agregación y re-delegación por huecos son parte del bucle de refinamiento iterativo.

questions.rationale: El coordinador concentra selección, enrutamiento, agregación y manejo de errores.

questions.stem: A documentation team creates a /generate-api-docs skill that reads source code files and produces Markdown API reference pages. The skill generates verbose output (200+ lines per endpoint) and should be available to every team member who clones the repository. How should the skill be configured?

options.text: Create a SKILL.md in ~/.claude/skills/ with context: fork frontmatter, and instruct each team member to copy it locally
options.explanation: ~/.claude/skills/ es de ámbito usuario y no está en control de versiones.

options.text: Create a SKILL.md in .claude/skills/ with context: fork, so it is shared via git and isolates the verbose output
options.explanation: .claude/skills/ es de proyecto y versionado; context: fork aísla la salida verbosa del presupuesto de contexto principal.

options.text: Add the documentation generation instructions to the root CLAUDE.md so they load automatically in every session
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md es para estándares siempre cargados, no para definiciones de comandos bajo demanda.

options.text: Create a SKILL.md in .claude/skills/ without any frontmatter, relying on the team to manually manage context overflow
options.explanation: Sin context: fork la salida verbosa inunda el contexto de la conversación principal.

questions.rationale: .claude/skills/ (versionado) + context: fork (aislamiento).

questions.stem: A research subagent queries an academic journal database for articles on renewable energy policy. The database responds successfully but returns zero matching articles. Meanwhile, a second subagent querying a government statistics API receives a connection timeout. The coordinator currently handles both cases identically by retrying three times. What should change?

options.text: Increase the retry count to five for both cases to give transient failures more time to resolve
options.explanation: La base de datos devolvió un resultado vacío válido: buscó y no encontró nada.

options.text: Add exponential backoff to all retries so the subagents wait progressively longer between attempts
options.explanation: El backoff mejora el reintento de fallos transitorios pero la consulta a la revista no necesita reintentos en absoluto.

options.text: Remove retries entirely and immediately escalate both failures to a human operator for investigation
options.explanation: Desproporcionado: el timeout es transitorio y el resultado vacío no es un fallo.

options.text: Distinguish access failures from valid empty results: retry the API timeout as a transient failure, but accept the zero-match journal response as a valid finding and annotate the coverage gap
options.explanation: Los fallos de acceso justifican reintento; los resultados vacíos válidos SON la respuesta.

questions.rationale: Separar fallo de acceso de resultado vacío válido.

questions.stem: A contract extraction system reports 96% overall accuracy. The team plans to auto-approve all extractions where model confidence exceeds 90%. A pilot reveals party name extraction achieves 99% accuracy but indemnification clause extraction only 71%, even though the model reports high confidence on both. What should they implement before automating?

options.text: Raise the automation confidence threshold from 90% to 99% to ensure only the most reliable extractions are automated.
options.explanation: Subir el umbral no arregla el problema de calibración: el modelo reporta alta confianza incluso donde acierta 71%.

options.text: Calibrate confidence thresholds per field type using labelled validation sets, and implement stratified sampling to continuously monitor accuracy by document type and field segment.
options.explanation: La calibración a nivel de campo expone la discrepancia entre confianza reportada y precisión real; el muestreo estratificado da monitoreo continuo.

options.text: Exclude indemnification clauses from automation entirely and continue automating all other field types at the 90% threshold.
options.explanation: Resuelve el problema conocido pero no detecta futuros problemas de calibración en otros campos.

options.text: Train a separate classification model to predict extraction accuracy before deciding whether to automate each extraction.
options.explanation: Añade complejidad de infraestructura cuando la solución es calibrar las puntuaciones existentes.

questions.rationale: Calibración por campo + muestreo estratificado continuo.

questions.stem: In a multi-agent research system the coordinator delegates to search and analysis subagents, then invokes a synthesis subagent. Reviewing the synthesis, the coordinator finds two claims with no supporting evidence and one sub-question left unanswered. What is the coordinator's correct next step?

options.text: Assess the synthesis for gaps, re-delegate targeted follow-up queries to fill them, then re-invoke synthesis with the new findings.
options.explanation: El coordinador es dueño del refinamiento iterativo: evaluar, re-delegar consultas dirigidas y re-sintetizar.

options.text: Accept the synthesis as final, since re-running the search and analysis subagents would push the coordinator past its configured iteration budget.
options.explanation: El tope de iteraciones es una red de seguridad, no una razón para dejar huecos conocidos.

options.text: Tell the synthesis subagent to fill the two evidence gaps and the open sub-question from its own knowledge, without any new delegation.
options.explanation: El subagente de síntesis no tiene herramientas ni fuentes para reunir evidencia nueva.

options.text: Restart the whole pipeline from scratch with a fresh coordinator to avoid contaminated context
options.explanation: Un reinicio completo tira hallazgos correctos y repite trabajo.

questions.rationale: Bucle de refinamiento iterativo, propiedad del coordinador.

questions.stem: A docs team maintains three content types in docs/api/, docs/architecture/, and docs/runbooks/, each with distinct formatting, terminology, and required sections. They want Claude Code to apply the correct standards automatically when editing any docs file, without loading all three rule sets in every session. What is the correct configuration architecture?

options.text: Place all three sets of rules in the root CLAUDE.md with clear section headings so Claude Code can identify which rules apply
options.explanation: El CLAUDE.md raíz carga en cada sesión, desperdiciando tokens y añadiendo un punto de fallo.

options.text: Create three rule files in .claude/rules/ with YAML frontmatter paths targeting each directory
options.explanation: Las reglas con globs cargan solo al editar archivos del directorio coincidente, conservando tokens y eliminando el riesgo de aplicar estándares incorrectos.

options.text: Place a separate CLAUDE.md file in each of docs/api/, docs/architecture/, and docs/runbooks/ with the type-specific rules
options.explanation: Los CLAUDE.md de directorio cargan según la jerarquía del directorio de trabajo, que normalmente es la raíz del repo.

options.text: Create three custom skills (/api-docs, /arch-docs, /runbook-docs) and require writers to invoke the correct one before editing
options.explanation: Depende de que el humano invoque la skill correcta; una elección equivocada aplica estándares erróneos en silencio.

questions.rationale: Reglas con alcance de ruta en .claude/rules/ con globs en frontmatter.

questions.stem: A coordinator spawns a research subagent to investigate market trends. The subagent returns detailed findings. The coordinator then needs to pass these findings to a synthesis subagent for report writing. However, the synthesis subagent produces a report that contradicts the research findings. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The synthesis subagent has a conflicting system prompt whose instructions override the research data it is handed.
options.explanation: Un system prompt en conflicto produciría salidas consistentemente erróneas en todas las peticiones.

options.text: The coordinator passes a summary instead of the full structured research output, so the synthesis agent fills gaps from its training data.
options.explanation: Los subagentes no comparten memoria. Si el coordinador solo pasa un resumen, el agente de síntesis rellena huecos con su entrenamiento.

options.text: The synthesis subagent has its own web search tool and keeps pulling contradictory information from the open web.
options.explanation: Un agente de síntesis no debería tener herramientas de búsqueda; eso viola el alcance de herramientas.

options.text: The two subagents run different model versions with separate training data, so they draw opposite conclusions.
options.explanation: Las diferencias de versión no causarían contradicciones con datos entregados explícitamente.

questions.rationale: El coordinador debe pasar la salida estructurada completa, no un resumen.
