concepts.answer: 1) Transient (timeouts, 5xx) — isRetryable: true. 2) Validation (bad input shape) — isRetryable: false. 3) Business (policy violations) — isRetryable: false. 4) Permission (unauthorized) — isRetryable: false, requires escalation.
concepts.note: OJO: el archivo de examen (EX-052) trata validation como retryable una vez el agente repara el input. Discrepancia a tener presente.

concepts.stem: What are the four tool_choice modes and when do you use each?
concepts.answer: auto: may emit text OR call any tool. any: must call SOME tool. {type:'tool', name:'X'}: must call that specific tool. none: cannot call any tool.

concepts.stem: When should you expose data via an MCP Resource vs. an MCP Tool?
concepts.answer: Resources expose static or semi-static content catalogs the agent reads to discover what data exists. Tools perform actions or specific queries. Use Resources to eliminate exploratory tool-call spam.

concepts.stem: What is the most effective way to help the model produce correctly formatted tool inputs?
concepts.answer: Clear, detailed parameter descriptions in the JSON schema — format expectations, example values, constraints.

concepts.stem: Where do .mcp.json and ~/.claude.json live, and what's the difference?
concepts.answer: .mcp.json is project-scoped and committed to version control. ~/.claude.json is user-scoped for personal/experimental servers. Use env-var expansion (${GITHUB_TOKEN}) instead of committing secrets.

concepts.stem: Describe the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and what each level is used for.
concepts.answer: User-level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md): personal preferences, NOT shared. Project-level (.claude/CLAUDE.md): version-controlled, team-wide. Directory-level (subdir/CLAUDE.md): scoped to a directory tree. More-specific levels add to, not replace, less-specific ones.

concepts.stem: Putting team-wide coding standards in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ensures everyone on the team follows them.
concepts.answer: False
concepts.note: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md es por usuario y no se comparte. Los estándares de equipo van en .claude/CLAUDE.md, commiteado al repo.

concepts.stem: How do you apply path-specific rules (e.g., 'all files under tests/ should use pytest')?
concepts.answer: Create files in .claude/rules/ with YAML frontmatter declaring glob 'paths' patterns. The rule loads only when the agent works on matching files.

concepts.stem: What are the key fields in a Skill's YAML frontmatter?
concepts.answer: name, description (used for skill selection), allowed-tools, context (e.g. 'fork' runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent), argument-hint.

concepts.stem: Skills vs. slash commands vs. CLAUDE.md — when do you use each?
concepts.answer: CLAUDE.md = universal standards always loaded. Slash commands = explicit parameterized prompts the user types. Skills = on-demand task-specific bundles with their own description, allowed-tools and optional isolated context. Skills auto-activate; commands are user-invoked.

concepts.stem: What flag enables Claude Code's non-interactive (headless) mode for CI/CD, and what flag formats the output for machine parsing?
concepts.answer: -p (or --print) for non-interactive mode; combine with --output-format json (often plus --json-schema or --max-turns) for machine-parseable output.

concepts.stem: Why should automated code review in CI run in a fresh/independent session, not a resumed one?
concepts.answer: To avoid confirmation bias and stale context. An independent session reviews the diff fresh, without inheriting the implementing agent's reasoning or anchored assumptions.

concepts.stem: What's the most reliable way to get consistent results from Claude on a repeated, format-sensitive task?
concepts.answer: Provide 2-3 concrete input/output examples showing the exact format, including edge cases. Examples beat prose descriptions of format.

concepts.stem: What do /memory and /compact do in Claude Code?
concepts.answer: /memory lists which CLAUDE.md and related memory files are currently loaded. /compact summarises prior turns to reduce context usage while preserving key state.

concepts.stem: What is the Explore subagent used for in Claude Code?
concepts.answer: Running verbose discovery work (file searches, dependency walks, large greps) in an isolated subagent so the main conversation's context isn't polluted with raw search output.

concepts.stem: When fixing multiple bugs found in a single review, when should you batch them vs. address them sequentially?
concepts.answer: Batch interacting/coupled issues together; sequence independent ones as separate focused iterations. Coupling drives batching; isolation drives sequencing.

concepts.stem: Name the core built-in file/code tools in Claude Code and what each is for.
concepts.answer: Read (file or range), Write (overwrite/create), Edit (anchored find/replace, needs unique target), Glob (find files by PATH pattern), Grep (search file CONTENTS), Bash (shell). Edit is preferred over Write; if Edit can't find a unique anchor, fall back to Read + Write.

concepts.stem: Why is 'flag comments only when claimed behavior directly contradicts actual code' better than 'check that comments are accurate'?
concepts.answer: Explicit categorical criteria give the model a concrete decision boundary. Vague instructions don't tell the model WHAT counts as a positive.

concepts.stem: How many few-shot examples are typically optimal for ambiguous tasks?
concepts.answer: 2-4 targeted examples covering the ambiguous boundaries, showing inputs, expected output and (when teaching judgment) the reasoning. Diminishing returns above ~5.

concepts.stem: What is the canonical mechanism for guaranteed structured output from Claude?
concepts.answer: tool_use with a JSON schema (especially strict: true), often combined with tool_choice = {type:'tool', name:'X'}. Asking the model to 'reply only in JSON' is unreliable.

concepts.stem: Why include nullable fields and 'unclear'/'other' enum values in extraction schemas?
concepts.answer: To prevent fabrication. Without a way to say 'missing' or 'ambiguous', the model guesses plausible values to fill mandatory fields.

concepts.stem: When are validation/retry loops effective, and when are they NOT?
concepts.answer: Effective for format/structural errors — send the failure back and the model fixes the shape. NOT effective when the underlying information is missing from the source; the schema must allow nullable/unclear so the model can report absence truthfully.

concepts.stem: What are the headline tradeoffs of the Message Batches API?
concepts.answer: Pros: ~50% cost discount. Cons: up to 24-hour window, no guaranteed SLA, no human-loop tool-use mid-batch, unusable for blocking workflows. Use custom_id to correlate inputs to outputs.

concepts.stem: What kinds of content should go in the system prompt vs. user messages?
concepts.answer: System: persona, role, durable rules, output-format requirements, tools. User: the actual task, dynamic context, per-request input. Stable content in system enables prompt caching.

concepts.stem: What is the 'lost in the middle' effect?
concepts.answer: LLMs reliably attend to the beginning and end of long inputs but under-weight the middle. Mitigations: key summaries at the top, explicit section headers, trimming verbose intermediate output, splitting long inputs into focused passes.

concepts.stem: How do you preserve source attribution through multi-agent synthesis?
concepts.answer: Assign a citation_id at the earliest discovery stage. The synthesis agent writes the narrative with inline tags like [src_001]. Pass a separate structured citation index alongside; never embed metadata in prose.

concepts.stem: Search agent returns 2024 stats; doc analysis returns 2021 stats. Synthesis flags them as conflicting instead of recognizing a growth trend. Best fix?
concepts.answer: Require publication_date in subagent output schemas and update synthesis to treat differing values across distinct dates as temporal progression. Reserve conflict_detected: true for differing values within the SAME time period.

concepts.stem: Self-reported model confidence scores are a reliable proxy for actual accuracy.
concepts.answer: False
concepts.note: La confianza emitida por el LLM está mal calibrada. Úsala como una señal más junto a análisis estratificado y muestreo, nunca como criterio único de automatización.

concepts.stem: When should a customer-support agent escalate to a human?
concepts.answer: 1) The customer explicitly asks. 2) Policy is silent or ambiguous. 3) The agent cannot make meaningful progress. NOT just because the customer is frustrated — sentiment alone is not an escalation trigger.

concepts.stem: When a subagent fails, what should it return to the coordinator?
concepts.answer: Structured error context: failure type, what was attempted, partial results, alternative approaches, recommended next action. NOT an empty result, NOT a generic exception, NOT silent suppression.

concepts.stem: What's the cost structure of Anthropic prompt caching?
concepts.answer: 5-minute cache write: 1.25x base input price. 1-hour cache write: 2x base. Cache read (hit): 0.1x base. A heavily cached prompt can be ~10x cheaper, but the first write costs more than uncached.
concepts.unverifiedNote: Depende de cifras no verificadas: precios de caché.

concepts.stem: What's the minimum cacheable token threshold for prompt caching?
concepts.answer: Roughly 1024-4096 tokens depending on the model. Below the minimum the request is processed without caching — no error, just no cache effect. Verify via cache_creation_input_tokens in the usage response.
concepts.unverifiedNote: Depende de cifras no verificadas: mínimos cacheables.

concepts.stem: Your cache hit rate is 0% even though you set cache_control. The breakpoint sits right before a timestamp that changes every request. Why no hits?
concepts.answer: Cache lookups match by content hash up to and including the breakpoint. If content immediately before the breakpoint changes every request, the hash never matches. Move the breakpoint to the last STABLE block and put dynamic content AFTER it.

concepts.stem: What kinds of changes invalidate the prompt cache?
concepts.answer: Changing the tools array invalidates tools + system + messages. Toggling web_search or citations invalidates system + messages. Changing extended-thinking settings or tool_choice invalidates messages. Adding/removing images invalidates messages. Invalidation cascades downward.
concepts.unverifiedNote: Depende de cifras no verificadas: cascada de invalidación.

concepts.stem: What is a 'case facts' block in long conversation context management?
concepts.answer: A persistent structured block near the top of the prompt holding durable facts (customer ID, account state, root cause, policy decisions), updated explicitly as facts are established, instead of relying on the model to remember earlier turns.

concepts.stem: When should you /compact a long conversation vs. start a fresh session with a structured summary?
concepts.answer: /compact when the conversation is still coherent and you want momentum. Fresh session + structured summary when prior tool results are stale (after a crash), when the agent has drifted, or when context is so polluted a clean reload is faster.

concepts.stem: How do you choose between Claude Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku?
concepts.answer: Opus: hardest reasoning, deep architectural decisions, ambiguity-heavy tasks — highest cost, slowest. Sonnet: production default for most agentic and code tasks. Haiku: high-throughput, latency-sensitive, simpler tasks. In multi-agent setups you can mix tiers.

concepts.stem: When does extended thinking help, and when is it overkill?
concepts.answer: Helps: math, multi-step logic, planning across many constraints, novel problems. Overkill: simple lookups, format-only tasks, latency-sensitive customer-facing turns. It consumes extra output tokens and adds latency.

concepts.stem: What does the Anthropic Citations feature do?
concepts.answer: Lets you mark documents in the prompt so Claude attaches exact citation spans (character positions or page references) to its claims, producing verifiable provenance instead of fabricated citations.

concepts.stem: When should you use the Files API vs. inlining document content in messages?
concepts.answer: Files API: large documents referenced multiple times, PDFs with native formatting, images at scale — upload once, reference by file_id. Inline: small one-off content, dynamic per-request data.

concepts.stem: What does MCP provide at a fundamental level?
concepts.answer: A standardized protocol connecting AI agents to external tools and data. An MCP server exposes Tools (actions/queries), Resources (readable content catalogs) and Prompts (reusable templates). Reduces N-to-M integration to N+M.

concepts.stem: What are key mitigations for prompt-injection attacks against agents?
concepts.answer: 1) Treat untrusted text as DATA, not instructions. 2) Enforce critical rules in code (hooks, preconditions). 3) Use structured schemas with enums/IDs rather than freeform fields. 4) Scope tool access narrowly per agent.

concepts.stem: Why scope each agent's tool access narrowly?
concepts.answer: Least privilege limits blast radius of mistakes and injection attacks, reduces decision complexity (4-5 tools vs 18+), and keeps reasoning focused on the role. A synthesis agent shouldn't have write/delete; a search agent shouldn't have refund-disburse.

concepts.stem: What does setting strict: true on a tool definition do?
concepts.answer: Guarantees Claude's tool_use input exactly matches your JSON schema — no extra fields, no missing required fields, correct types. Pairs with forced tool_choice for deterministic structured output.

concepts.stem: Difference between Anthropic's server tools and client tools?
concepts.answer: Server tools (web_search, code_execution, web_fetch, tool_search) run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Client tools (user-defined, or bash/text_editor) run in your app: Claude returns tool_use, you execute and send tool_result back.

concepts.stem: Which Anthropic Academy (Skilljar) courses map most directly to exam content?
concepts.answer: Building with the Claude API (~8h), Introduction to MCP, MCP: Advanced Topics, Claude Code in Action, Introduction to Agent Skills. 15-20h for experienced devs, 30-40h for newcomers.
concepts.note: Material de estudio, no contenido examinable.

concepts.stem: During research on renewable energy adoption, a web search agent returns 2024 statistics while a document analysis agent returns 2021 statistics. The synthesis agent incorrectly flags these as contradictory rather than recognizing a growth trend. What single change best enables correct interpretation?
concepts.answer: Require publication_date in structured outputs and update synthesis instructions so differing values across distinct dates read as temporal progression; reserve conflict_detected: true for the same time period.
